scope: Existing six source-bound cervical-disc MRI drafts only; not clinical approval or geometry change

oldTopic.body: On real MRI, follow the cervical disc across sagittal and axial sections and relate its posterior margin to the canal and foramina.
bullets: Disc signal and contour require sequence-specific assessment; this surface cannot establish degeneration, extrusion or cord involvement.
Use the retained source name and independently confirm the patient level; a nearby landmark is not a registration.

newTopic.body: Use the cervical disc surface as a locator between its source-labelled neighbouring bones, not as a patient MR slice. On actual cervical MRI, confirm the vertebral level on sagittal images before comparing the corresponding axial images. Follow the selected disc toward its posterior margin and examine the canal, spinal cord and surrounding fluid space on the acquired sequences.
bullets: At the same level, inspect both neural foramina where the examination shows them adequately; a single midline image does not describe their full extent. Check coverage, sequence contrast and image quality before interpreting what is or is not visible.

A source name does not number a patient’s vertebrae, and a model colour does not reproduce MR signal. This selection is one exterior disc surface: it does not map internal disc layers, a cervical root course, cord signal or a patient-specific disc contour.
Neither a possible extrusion nor neural compression can be established from mesh proximity or an exploded view. Interpret the actual examination; no scan-to-model registration is supplied.
